basis: Cash basis, continuing operations, full year ended 30 June 2026 versus full year ended 30 June 2025, using FY25 divisional comparatives restated in the FY26 Profit Announcement to conform to the current-period presentation. Loan impairment expense is identical on the statutory basis for both periods.

drivers.name: Retail Banking Services
drivers.narrative: Expense increased from the restated FY25 comparator of A$272m to A$378m. CBA attributes the combined increase primarily to increased geopolitical risk, macroeconomic uncertainty and rising cost-of-living pressures. The document does not split the A$106m among those causes.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 34, "An increase in Retail Banking Services of $106 million to an expense of $378 million")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 65, "mainly driven by increased geopolitical risk, macroeconomic uncertainty, and rising cost-of-living pressures")

drivers.name: Business Banking
drivers.narrative: Expense decreased from the restated FY25 comparator of A$355m to A$310m. Lower individually assessed provision charges, including more write-backs, were partly offset by higher collective provisions for portfolio growth, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty. CBA does not quantify the internal offsets.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 34, "A decrease in Business Banking of $45 million to an expense of $310 million")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 69, "lower individually assessed provision charges, including an increase in write-backs, partly offset by higher collective provisions")

drivers.name: Institutional Banking and Markets
drivers.narrative: Expense decreased from A$49m to A$33m. Releases of individually assessed provisions more than offset higher collective provisions for increased geopolitical risk, macroeconomic uncertainty and portfolio growth. CBA does not quantify the two legs separately.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 34, "A decrease in Institutional Banking and Markets of $16 million to an expense of $33 million")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 73, "release of individually assessed provisions, partly offset by higher collective provisions")

drivers.name: New Zealand
drivers.narrative: The Group's Australian-dollar expense increased from A$55m to A$66m. Higher collective provisions reflected a weaker unemployment outlook, increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty; lower individually assessed provisions and consumer-finance write-offs partly offset this. CBA does not quantify those internal offsets or the translation effect.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 34, "An increase in New Zealand of $11 million to an expense of $66 million")
(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 79, "higher collective provisions reflecting deterioration in the unemployment outlook, and increased geopolitical risk and macroeconomic uncertainty")

drivers.name: Corporate Centre and Other
drivers.narrative: A FY25 benefit of A$5m became a FY26 expense of A$1m, increasing Group expense by A$6m. CBA gives no further causal attribution, so the underlying driver is unquantified.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 82, "Loan impairment expense was $1 million, an increase of $6 million on the prior year.")

accounting_cross_check.interpretation: This independent accounting bridge reconciles exactly to the reported movement. It is a cross-check, not an additional set of drivers to add to the divisional bridge.

disagreements.values: The FY25 Profit Announcement originally reported Retail Banking Services at A$274m and Business Banking at A$353m; the FY26 Profit Announcement restates them to A$272m and A$355m. The Group total remains A$726m.
disagreements.preferred: Use the FY26 document's restated comparatives, because it explicitly says the comparative information was restated to conform to the current-period presentation. That produces the disclosed contributions of +A$106m and -A$45m; using the originally published FY25 divisional values would produce +A$104m and -A$43m, with no change to the A$62m Group movement.
citations: (CBA-FY25-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 34, "Retail Banking Services 274"; "Business Banking 353"; "Loan impairment expense/(benefit) 726")

(CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 34, "Retail Banking Services 378 272"; "Business Banking 310 355"; "Comparative information has been restated to conform to presentation in the current period.")

disagreements.values: The Profit Announcement and ASX announcement round the year-on-year increase to 9%; the Results Presentation shows 8.5%.
disagreements.preferred: Prefer the exact A$62m movement for attribution. The percentage difference is rounding: A$62m divided by A$726m is 8.5% to one decimal and 9% to the nearest whole percent.
citations: (CBA-FY26-profit-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 34, "an increase of $62 million or 9% on the prior year")
(CBA-FY26-asx-announcement.pdf, PDF p. 2, "$788m (Loan loss rate 8bpts) 9% on FY25")

limitations: Confidence scores are analyst judgements, not figures disclosed by CBA.

CBA quantifies the divisional bridge but does not allocate each division's movement among the macroeconomic, geopolitical, portfolio-growth, arrears, individual-provision and write-back causes; those sub-drivers are therefore unquantified.
The Corporate Centre and Other movement has no disclosed causal explanation beyond the divisional amount.

The New Zealand contribution is reported in Australian dollars at Group level, while the detailed ASB discussion is in New Zealand dollars; the supplied documents do not quantify the foreign-exchange translation effect on the year-on-year movement.
Arrears and provision-coverage indicators corroborate direction but are not used as dollar attributions because CBA does not map them mechanically to loan impairment expense.
